content.content:
13:Input on the left, send button on the right.
15:Sending sends the prompt in the selected tab's mode, as the [PromptSendingScope](../sending/PromptSendingScope.md) says. While the harness is working, the send button on the Code, Chain, and Spec tabs reads "Queue", since the prompt will queue. On the Ask tab it always reads "Send", because a question is never queued. The button is only disabled while the input is empty.
23:##### Split Button
25:The send button is a split button: the send or queue button itself, and joined to its right, a narrow half with a chevron that opens a menu of other ways to send the prompt, above the button, its right edge lined up with the button's. The chevron half is disabled whenever the send half is, and while a preview shows, and its tooltip says it shows more ways to send, with its shortcut.
36:- "Queue", with a list icon, which queues the prompt rather than sending it, even while the harness is free, as the queue of the [PromptEditor](../PromptEditor.md) says; like the send button, it clears the input. On the Ask tab it is disabled, since a question never queues, and the highlight passes over it
40:Editing a queued prompt, from the queue of the [PromptEditor](../PromptEditor.md), sets aside the prompt being written, its attachments, and the selected tab, and puts the queued prompt's text in the input, its attachments above it, and its mode's tab selected, with the cursor at the end of the text. Above the attachments, a row with a pencil icon reads "Editing queued prompt N", its place in the queue, and at its right, muted, "Ctrl+Enter to save · Esc to cancel" (with ⌘ on macOS). The send button reads "Save", its tooltip saying it saves the queued prompt, and the send menu isn't offered.
45:Preview Compiled Prompt compiles the prompt as it would be sent from the selected tab, its hidden anchor, attachments, and mode's system prompt included, without sending it, saving it to the history, or building the spec first. In place of the text input, the chat input then shows what the harness would receive: the compiled prompt, as a sent task's compiled prompt is shown, beneath a row reading "Compiled prompt" with, at its right, muted, "Ctrl+Enter to send · Esc to edit" (with ⌘ on macOS). While it compiles, the row shows a spinner and "Compiling…"; a prompt that fails to compile shows why, in the theme's error colour, in place of the compiled prompt. The preview grows with what it shows, up to 40% of the window's height, and scrolls beyond that. The tabs, attachments, and send button stay as they are.
46:The preview has keyboard focus. <Ctrl+Enter> (<Cmd+Enter> on macOS), or the send button, sends the prompt just as sending from the text input would, and the chat input goes back to an empty text input. <Escape> goes back to the text input with the prompt and attachments as they were, the cursor where it was. Switching tabs while previewing goes back to the text input too, since the prompt would compile differently.
51:overview: The input and send button live inside the body of a tab bar, using gpui-kit's default tab styling. There is a tab for each of the [PromptModesScope](../modes/PromptModesScope.md), in their order: Code, Chain, Spec, and Ask. Code, Spec, and Ask are ordinary tabs. Chain is also a tab, just a small one, because it only shows an icon. All four sit flush against each other with no extra gaps, and no tab has more padding than a normal tab.
61:session: At the far right of the bar, at the right end of the help text, sits how much context the selected tab's conversation holds, then a New conversation button. The questions of the Ask tab have a conversation of their own, and the other tabs share the tasks', as the [HarnessIntegrationScope](../../harness-integration/HarnessIntegrationScope.md) says, so the figure is the Ask tab's conversation while it is selected, and the tasks' on any other tab.
63:New conversation is a small ghost button with a sparkles icon, reading "New conversation". Pressing it starts a new conversation for the selected tab: the tasks' on Code, Chain, and Spec, the questions' on Ask. The next run in that tab, or in any tab sharing its conversation, starts a new one with no context instead of carrying on, and the figure reads "Context 0". A run of the conversation left that is still going finishes as it would, but neither it nor the project's history brings that conversation back, even once the project is closed and opened again, as the [HarnessIntegrationScope](../../harness-integration/HarnessIntegrationScope.md) says.
66:colour: The selected tab and the tab body holding the input are tinted the colour of its mode, of the [PromptModesScope](../modes/PromptModesScope.md). With Chain selected, Code, Spec, and the body are all purple. The colour transitions smoothly whenever the selected tab changes, straight from the old tab's colour to the new one's. The tabs wrap around, so pressing <Ctrl+Tab> on Ask fades green straight to Code's red, and <Ctrl+Shift+Tab> on Code fades red straight to Ask's green; neither lights up Chain or Spec on the way.
77:Once a question is complete, it opens onto a heading, with its status and first line, above its full task table, in the [AnswerDrawerScope](../answer-drawer/AnswerDrawerScope.md), which it fills, the table scrolling once it is taller, with its lock to the bottom off to start with. Only one question is open at a time: opening another closes the one open back down to its row. An open question leaves the stack for the drawer. Clicking an open question's heading closes it down to its row in the stack, and clicking a finished question's row opens it again. Each question has a close button, which removes it and stops it if it is still running, leaving the others running. A closed question becomes a previous answer.
93:The text of an answer being viewed, in the answer drawer, whether an open question or a previous answer, can be selected by dragging across it, as any text can. A drag that selects text ending within the drawer shows a [SelectionPopoverScope](../../../ui/components/selection-popover/SelectionPopoverScope.md) with two buttons: "Copy", with a copy icon, and "Attach to prompt", with a paperclip icon.
98:What is attached to the prompt is listed above the text input, between the tabs and the input, one row per attachment in the order they were attached, and only while there is anything attached. An attached piece of text shows a quote icon, the text's first line cut off with an ellipsis, and, when it runs to more than one line, how many lines it has, muted, and at the right end a small button with a cross, whose tooltip says it removes the attachment, which removes just that one.
111:The text input is a [GrowingTextInputScope](../../../ui/components/growing-text-input/GrowingTextInputScope.md) growing to 12 rows at most. Its single row lines up with the send button.
153:Drawn in the [ThemeScope](../../../ui/theme/ThemeScope.md): its surfaces, text, lines, accent, and status colours are the theme's roles, named as the theme names them, in both dark and light mode, never colours of its own.

use /lib
use /ui
from /ui/components/growing-text-input import GrowingTextInputScope
from /ui/components/selection-popover import SelectionPopoverScope
from /scope/harness-integration import HarnessIntegrationScope
from /scope/harness-integration/catalog import HarnessCatalogScope
from /scope/lsp import LSP
from /scope/prompt-mode/answer-drawer import AnswerDrawerScope
from /scope/prompt-mode/message-list import MessageList
from /scope/prompt-mode/mode-system-prompts import ModeSystemPromptsScope
from /scope/prompt-mode/modes import PromptModesScope
from /scope/prompt-mode/sending import PromptSendingScope
from /ui/components/history-list import HistoryListScope
from /ui/components/task-table import TaskTableScope
from /scope/prompt-mode import PromptEditor
from /scope/open-projects import OpenProjectsScope
from /shape/ChatInput import ChatInputInstruction

export ui-component ChatInputScope:
    concept: {ChatInputConcept}

concept ChatInputConcept:
    pitch:
        A multi-line, syntax-highlighted textbox that accepts plain text as well
        as snippets of Piton.

    shape: {ChatInputShape}

shape ChatInputShape:
    description:
        Input on the left, send button on the right.

        <Enter> allows for creating new lines, like Ctrl/Cmd+Enter sends it to
        the ${HarnessIntegrationScope}

        Sending sends the prompt in the selected tab's mode, as the
        @{PromptSendingScope} says. While the harness is working, the send
        button on the Code, Chain, and Spec tabs reads "Queue", since the prompt
        will queue. On the Ask tab it always reads "Send", because a question is
        never queued. The button is only disabled while the input is empty.

    instructions:
        - @{ChatInputInstruction}

    sendOptions:
        splitButton:
            The send button is a split button: the send or queue button itself,
            and joined to its right, a narrow half with a chevron that opens a
            menu of other ways to send the prompt, above the button, its right
            edge lined up with the button's. The chevron half is disabled
            whenever the send half is, and while a preview shows, and its
            tooltip says it shows more ways to send, with its shortcut.

        keyboard:
            <Ctrl+Shift+Enter> (<Cmd+Shift+Enter> on macOS) in the chat input
            opens the menu with its first option highlighted, and does nothing
            while the input is empty or a preview shows. While it is open, the
            text keeps focus, <Up> and <Down> move the highlight, wrapping
            around, <Enter> picks the highlighted option, and <Escape> closes
            the menu, as does pressing <Ctrl+Shift+Enter> again or the mouse
            anywhere outside it. Each option highlights on hover, and clicking
            one picks it.

        options:
            The menu's options, in order:
            - "Preview Compiled Prompt", with an eye icon
            - "Queue", with a list icon, which queues the prompt rather than sending it, even while the harness is free, as the queue of the @{PromptEditor} says; like the send button, it clears the input. On the Ask tab it is disabled, since a question never queues, and the highlight passes over it

    editingQueued:
        Editing a queued prompt, from the queue of the @{PromptEditor}, sets
        aside the prompt being written, its attachments, and the selected tab,
        and puts the queued prompt's text in the input, its attachments above
        it, and its mode's tab selected, with the cursor at the end of the text.
        Above the attachments, a row with a pencil icon reads
        "Editing queued prompt N", its place in the queue, and at its right,
        muted, "Ctrl+Enter to save · Esc to cancel" (with ⌘ on macOS). The send
        button reads "Save", its tooltip saying it saves the queued prompt, and
        the send menu isn't offered.

        Everything in the input works as ever while editing, tabs included.
        <Ctrl+Enter> (<Cmd+Enter> on macOS), or Save, saves the edit, in the tab
        selected then, and <Escape>, when nothing else in the input takes it,
        cancels it. Either way, the prompt that was set aside comes back just as
        it was. Saving an empty prompt isn't possible, just as sending one
        isn't. Editing another queued prompt meanwhile first cancels the edit in
        progress; so does switching projects.

    preview:
        Preview Compiled Prompt compiles the prompt as it would be sent from the
        selected tab, its hidden anchor, attachments, and mode's system prompt
        included, without sending it, saving it to the history, or building the
        spec first. In place of the text input, the chat input then shows what
        the harness would receive: the compiled prompt, as a sent task's
        compiled prompt is shown, beneath a row reading "Compiled prompt" with,
        at its right, muted, "Ctrl+Enter to send · Esc to edit" (with ⌘ on
        macOS). While it compiles, the row shows a spinner and "Compiling…"; a
        prompt that fails to compile shows why, in the theme's error colour, in
        place of the compiled prompt. The preview grows with what it shows, up
        to 40% of the window's height, and scrolls beyond that. The tabs,
        attachments, and send button stay as they are.

        The preview has keyboard focus. <Ctrl+Enter> (<Cmd+Enter> on macOS), or
        the send button, sends the prompt just as sending from the text input
        would, and the chat input goes back to an empty text input. <Escape>
        goes back to the text input with the prompt and attachments as they
        were, the cursor where it was. Switching tabs while previewing goes back
        to the text input too, since the prompt would compile differently.

    tabs:
        overview:
            The input and send button live inside the body of a tab bar, using
            gpui-kit's default tab styling. There is a tab for each of the
            @{PromptModesScope}, in their order: Code, Chain, Spec, and Ask.
            Code, Spec, and Ask are ordinary tabs. Chain is also a tab, just a
            small one, because it only shows an icon. All four sit flush against
            each other with no extra gaps, and no tab has more padding than a
            normal tab.

            The chat input starts in the combined mode: Chain is selected, so
            Code and Spec are selected together, and a prompt sent before
            switching tabs changes the code and the spec together.

            Pressing <Ctrl+Tab> while in the chat input cycles from Code to
            Chain to Spec to Ask and back to Code, <Ctrl+Shift+Tab> the other
            way, and focus remains in the chat input. It is <Ctrl> on macOS too,
            not <Cmd>.

            <Tab> and <Shift+Tab> don't switch tabs, and don't indent the text
            either: they move keyboard focus out of the chat input to the next
            or previous control, as they do everywhere else. While the
            completion menu is open, <Tab> is still the menu's.

        chain:
            Chain is a tab with unusual behaviour. It shows an icon rather than
            a label, reading "Code and Spec" as its tooltip, and selecting it
            selects both Code and Spec. It never shows a focus outline, and its
            icon looks evenly spaced between Code and Spec whichever of the two
            is selected.

            Unselected, it shows a broken chain dimmed to 50% opacity, and sits
            between Code and Spec like any other tab, overlapping neither of
            them.

            In combined mode, with Chain selected, Chain has no line along its
            bottom, just as the joined Code and Spec beneath it have none. In
            separate mode, unselected, it has one, like any other unselected
            tab: the tab bar's bottom line runs beneath it, the same colour and
            thickness, in the same place, as beneath any other unselected tab,
            at any display scale. This holds at every
            window size and display scale, in light and dark mode: in combined
            mode nothing draws a line beneath Chain at all, rather than a line
            being drawn and then hidden, since a hidden line can show again
            wherever rounding to the display's pixels uncovers it.

            Selected, it shows a joined chain at full opacity. Selecting it
            animates as though it took a margin of -50% of its own width on both
            its left and right sides: Code and Spec slide together until they
            meet underneath it, so it ends up sitting on top of both.
            Deselecting it animates them apart again. While Chain is selected,
            Code and Spec both show as selected and read as a single unified
            tab, with no line between them. Chain itself has a transparent
            background and no left or right borders, so the joined Code and Spec
            show through underneath it.

        help:
            To the right of the tabs, filling the rest of the bar, a line of
            help text says what the selected tab is for, and changes as soon as
            another tab is selected. It is extra small and dimmer than muted
            text, set a little apart from the last tab, so it reads as a quiet
            note about the tab rather than as another tab. It is cut off rather
            than wrapped when the bar is too narrow.

            It reads what the selected tab's mode is for, as the
            @{PromptModesScope} says.

        session:
            At the far right of the bar, at the right end of the help text,
            sits how much context the selected tab's conversation holds, then a
            New conversation button. The questions of the Ask tab have a
            conversation of their own, and the other tabs share the tasks', as
            the @{HarnessIntegrationScope} says, so the figure is the Ask tab's
            conversation while it is selected, and the tasks' on any other tab.

            The figure reads "Context", then the number of tokens, short and
            extra small, muted: "850", "42.1k", "123k", or "1.2M", to a decimal
            place below a hundred of a unit. It follows each reply as the
            harness reports it. While the next prompt would start a new
            conversation, as when the project has none yet or New conversation
            was just pressed, it reads "Context 0". Its tooltip says how many
            tokens the conversation the next prompt carries on holds, or that
            the next prompt starts a new conversation.

            New conversation is a small ghost button with a sparkles icon,
            reading "New conversation". Pressing it starts a new conversation
            for the selected tab: the tasks' on Code, Chain, and Spec, the
            questions' on Ask. The next run in that tab, or in any tab sharing
            its conversation, starts a new one with no context instead of
            carrying on, and the figure reads "Context 0". A run of the
            conversation left that is still going finishes as it would, but
            neither it nor the project's history brings that conversation back,
            even once the project is closed and opened again, as the
            @{HarnessIntegrationScope} says.

            Its tooltip says which conversation it resets:
            "Start a new conversation for tasks" or
            "Start a new conversation for questions". It is disabled while that conversation has nothing to
            carry on, its tooltip then saying the next task, or question,
            already starts a new conversation; and while a run in it is under
            way, a task on Code, Chain, or Spec, or any question on Ask, its
            tooltip then saying it waits for that run to finish.

            Both sit on the bar's bottom line, which runs beneath them as it does
            beneath the help text, and neither is cut off: the help text gives
            way to them when the bar is narrow.

        colour:
            The selected tab and the tab body holding the input are tinted the
            colour of its mode, of the @{PromptModesScope}. With Chain selected,
            Code, Spec, and the body are all purple. The colour transitions
            smoothly whenever the selected tab changes, straight from the old
            tab's colour to the new one's. The tabs wrap around, so pressing
            <Ctrl+Tab> on Ask fades green straight to Code's red, and
            <Ctrl+Shift+Tab> on Code fades red straight to Ask's green; neither
            lights up Chain or Spec on the way.

    systemPrompt:
        The selected tab is the mode a prompt is sent in, and each mode's system
        prompt is sent with it, as the @{ModeSystemPromptsScope} says.

    ask:
        Ask is for simply asking a question, which runs as the
        @{PromptModesScope} says. Any number of questions can be asked, and they
        all run at the same time; asking another never stops or waits for one
        already running.

        Each question's progress and results are shown in a @{TaskTableScope}.
        The questions stack directly above the tabs, the newest nearest them, in
        a column that pushes the message list up to make room rather than
        covering it, so none of a running task's progress is ever hidden behind
        them. Each slides up out of the chat input with an animation as it is
        asked, the message list giving way above it. While the harness works on
        a question, it is a single row showing the latest thing the harness did.
        A finished question is a row with its status and first line.

        Once a question is complete, it opens onto a heading, with its status
        and first line, above its full task table, in the @{AnswerDrawerScope},
        which it fills, the table scrolling once it is taller, with its lock to
        the bottom off to start with. Only one question is open at a time:
        opening another closes the one open back down to its row. An open
        question leaves the stack for the drawer. Clicking an open question's
        heading closes it down to its row in the stack, and clicking a finished
        question's row opens it again. Each question has a close button, which
        removes it and stops it if it is still running, leaving the others
        running. A closed question becomes a previous answer.

    answerSteps:
        For a question, only the answer matters, so wherever a finished
        question's task table is shown, an open question and a previous answer,
        the table collapses the steps leading up to the answer, as the
        @{TaskTableScope} says. A question closed into the previous answers
        starts collapsed again. Tasks are never collapsed like this: see the
        @{MessageList}.

    previousAnswers:
        Previous answers are a @{HistoryListScope}, shown only while the Ask tab
        is selected, at the top of the questions stacked above the tabs. It
        lists every question asked before and closed: those saved with the
        project and those closed since. Its row reads "No previous answers",
        "1 previous answer", or "N previous answers", and while expanded,
        "Back to the questions". Expanded, the row and the list go into the
        @{AnswerDrawerScope}, sliding up from on top of any question rows still
        in the stack. The questions asked from now on carry on the conversation
        the latest of them left off.

    answerDrawer: @{AnswerDrawerScope}

    selectingAnswerText:
        The text of an answer being viewed, in the answer drawer, whether an
        open question or a previous answer, can be selected by dragging across
        it, as any text can. A drag that selects text ending within the drawer
        shows a @{SelectionPopoverScope} with two buttons: "Copy", with a copy
        icon, and "Attach to prompt", with a paperclip icon.

        Copy puts the selected text on the clipboard. Attach to prompt adds it
        to the prompt as an attachment. Either one clears the selection. The
        popover also closes when the drawer closes.

    attachments:
        What is attached to the prompt is listed above the text input, between
        the tabs and the input, one row per attachment in the order they were
        attached, and only while there is anything attached. An attached piece
        of text shows a quote icon, the text's first line cut off with an
        ellipsis, and, when it runs to more than one line, how many lines it
        has, muted, and at the right end a small button with a cross, whose
        tooltip says it removes the attachment, which removes just that one.

        Attachments belong to the prompt being written, not to a tab: switching
        tabs keeps them all, and they go with the prompt whichever tab it is
        sent from. When the prompt is sent, its attachments are sent along with
        it and the list empties, as the text input does. A queued prompt keeps
        the attachments it was sent with.

    projects:
        The questions stacked above the tabs, the open answer, and the previous
        answers belong to their project, as the @{OpenProjectsScope} says:
        switching projects shows those of the project switched to, while the
        questions of other projects carry on running in the background. The
        prompt being written, its attachments, and the selected tab stay as they
        are across a switch, and are sent to the project on screen.

    escape:
        Pressing <Escape> while in the chat input takes focus out of the chat
        input.

    growToFit:
        The text input is a @{GrowingTextInputScope} growing to 12 rows at most.
        Its single row lines up with the send button.

    autoFocus:
        The chat input should be auto-focused.

    syntaxHighlighting:
        Syntax highlighting will be supported via the [Tree Sitter
        Grammar](https://github.com/piton-lang/tree-sitter-piton)

    lsp: @{LSP}

    harnessMentions:
        overview:
            Typing `/` offers the harness's skills and commands, and typing `@`
            offers its agents, the way they are offered in the harness itself.
            The placeholder mentions both.

        trigger:
            A mention starts at `/` or `@` at the start of the input or after
            whitespace, so paths and email addresses never open it, and an at
            sign followed by an opening curly brace is still a Piton reference.
            Completions are requested after typing the `/` or `@`, and after
            each letter, digit, hyphen, underscore, or colon of the name that
            follows. Only inside a mention are a slash or a hyphen a trigger;
            outside of one they never reach the @{LSP}.

        offered:
            The skills, commands, and agents offered are the
            @{HarnessCatalogScope}'s. Each shows whether it is a skill, command,
            or agent, and its description as documentation when it has one.
            Results are narrowed and ordered like Piton completions: matches at
            the start of a name before matches anywhere in it, then by name.

        accepting:
            Accepting one inserts it as a mention, as the @{HarnessCatalogScope}
            says, in place of what was typed of it. Mentions work without the
            @{LSP}.

    hiddenAnchor:
        While the user will be able to type plain text, behind the scenes,
        they'll be typing into a randomly-named piton anchor with a userPrompt
        property.  It's this compiled anchor that will be send to the
        @{HarnessIntegrationScope}

        escaping:
            A prompt may hold anything, text pasted into it included, so it
            isn't written into the anchor as Piton prose, where braces, quotes,
            colons, leading dashes, code fences, comments, indentation, and
            backslashes all mean something. Its userPrompt is a list with an
            item per line of the prompt, in order, and each line a list of its
            pieces: the text between references as a quoted string, with
            quotes, backslashes, and each dollar-brace escaped, so nothing in it
            is interpolated or evaluated; and each at-brace or dollar-brace
            around a dotted path of identifiers whose first name is imported as
            a reference of its own. A reference to a name that isn't imported,
            such as a pasted shell variable, is only text. An empty line is a
            single empty string. The compiled userPrompt is the pieces of each
            line joined together, and the lines joined by line breaks, so what
            the harness receives is exactly what was typed or pasted, line for
            line, with each reference resolved. The systemPrompt is written the
            same way. A prompt saved as prose by an earlier version still reads
            back.

        autoImports:
            The names a prompt uses are imported however the prompt got there,
            typed, completed, or pasted. What `piton lsp` is shown while the
            prompt is typed is the prompt as prose, line for line and position
            for position as typed, but with anything outside a reference other
            than letters, digits, and spaces between words blanked out,
            character for character. Pasted text with an unclosed quote or
            brace, a code fence, deeper indentation, or what would be a comment
            then never stops the server finding the names that need importing,
            both as completions are offered and when the prompt is sent.

        attachedText:
            A prompt with attached text gives the hidden anchor an attachedText
            property: a list with an item per attached piece of text, in the
            order they were attached. Since attached text is taken as it is, not
            as Piton, each item is itself a list of the text's lines, each a
            quoted string, with quotes and backslashes escaped, so nothing in it
            is interpolated or evaluated. A prompt with nothing attached has no
            attachedText property.

            What the harness receives is the compiled userPrompt followed by the
            attached text: a line reading "Attached text:", then each piece as a
            fenced code block, whose fence is longer than any run of backticks
            in the text itself. This is also the compiled prompt shown in the
            task's header.

content.text:
The send button is now the selected tab's colour at full strength: red on Code, purple on Chain, blue on Spec, green on Ask. The tab and the body behind it keep the faint 10% tint of the same colour, so the button stands out. The spec builds, clippy is clean, and 245 of 246 tests pass; the one failure is the same `spec-reading.md` issue as last time. I haven't looked at it in the running app.

- **Both halves are coloured.** The Send/Queue part and the chevron part share the colour.
- **Text:** the label and chevron use the theme's existing text colour for solid colours. That's dark text in dark mode, where the colours are light, and white in light mode.
- **Hover, press and divider:** hovering or pressing makes it a little darker in dark mode and a little lighter in light mode. The line between the two halves is the pressed shade.
- **Disabled:** when the input is empty, it fades the usual disabled way but keeps the colour.

**Changed files:**
- **Spec:** `spec/scope/prompt-mode/chat-input/index.pi`, under `colour`.
- **Code:** `src/chat_input.rs`, plus a new test that checks the button's colour against every tab in both themes.

**It doesn't fade between colours.** When you switch tabs, the tab and body fade smoothly but the button changes colour at once. The button library only accepts fixed colours, so fading it too would mean drawing the button's colour ourselves. I can do that if the jump looks wrong.

**Still open from last time:** `system_prompts::tests::defaults_are_this_repositorys_templates` fails because `spec-reading.md` has `...` where the test and spec expect `…`. Do you want to keep `...` (I'll update the test and spec to match) or go back to `…`?
